Give each named [covariate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#def-covariate) a letter that suggests what it measures,
and subscript its regression coefficient with that same letter.
A reader then knows which covariate a coefficient multiplies without looking it up.
In a group that uses shared macros (see [Using shared macros](#using-shared-macros)),
write the coefficient of a covariate $A$ as `\coef{A}`, which prints $\coef{A}$.

Keep the numbered covariate $x_j$, with coefficient $\coef{x_j}$,
for statements that hold for any covariate in a model with $p$ of them,
where no particular covariate is meant,
as in the [linear regression model](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/correlation-regression.html#def-linear-regression).
Do not number the covariates of a worked example.
A numbered coefficient such as $\coef{1}$ makes the reader count positions in the model,
and the count changes when a covariate is added or dropped.

::: {#exm-covariate-symbols}

## Coefficients named by their covariates

Consider the birthweight data of @dobson4e [Example 2.2.2]:
the birthweights, in grams, and estimated gestational ages, in weeks, of male and female infants born in one hospital.
Let $Y$ be birthweight,
let the [covariate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/model-validation.html#def-covariate) $M$ indicate a male infant,
and let the covariate $A$ be gestational age.

> ❌ $\condE{Y}{X_1 = x_1, X_2 = x_2} = \intcoef + \coef{1} x_1 + \coef{2} x_2$, where $X_1$ is the male indicator and $X_2$ is gestational age.
>
> ✅ $\condE{Y}{M = m, A = a} = \intcoef + \coef{M} m + \coef{A} a$.

In the ✅ version, the coefficient $\coef{A}$ multiplies the gestational age $a$,
so a reader sees at once that $\coef{A}$ is the difference in mean birthweight per week of gestational age,
holding sex fixed.

:::
